decisions.decision: How is B08 split into plan folders?
decisions.ruling: One per language, 6 folders in a chain: 1) plugin base + CSS/Tailwind, 2) YAML, 3) TOML, 4) HTML, 5) Astro, 6) TypeScript. Each later folder requires folder 1.
decisions.rejected: Two folders (base + CSS, then all others); one folder for all 6 languages

decisions.decision: Which rule namespace do our own rules use?
decisions.ruling: Keep current names: our plugins register under the same keys (tailwindcss/, html/, yml/, toml/, astro/, @typescript-eslint/). No consumer override breaks, and the golden snapshots keep the same rule names, which proves parity.
decisions.rejected: One new namespace for all rules; a new key per language (both break consumer overrides: a MAJOR release)

decisions.decision: Does tailwind-csstree stay as a dependency?
decisions.ruling: Write our own Tailwind 4 syntax for CSSTree in the repo. Zero new packages.
decisions.rejected: Keep tailwind-csstree 0.4.2 (0 deps, by the ESLint author, Apache-2.0)

decisions.decision: Which Tailwind rules do we port?
decisions.ruling: All 18 rules of @poupe/eslint-plugin-tailwindcss 0.3.1 except the Vue-only rule require-reference-in-vue (D22).
decisions.rejected: Only the 15 rules the preset enables; all 19

decisions.decision: How do we credit the MIT code that we port?
decisions.ruling: One notices file: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md with the license text and copyright of each source, added to the files of package.json so it ships. Each ported file gets a one-line header that names its source. Later plans add their entries to the same file.
decisions.rejected: The full MIT notice in a comment in each file; a clean-room rewrite from docs only

decisions.decision: What test bar does each ported rule meet?
decisions.ruling: A RuleTester test for each rule in tests/unit/, with valid and invalid cases ported from the upstream test files at tag v0.3.1 where they exist, plus each fix output. New tests for the 5 rules with no upstream test. The golden snapshots must keep the same problems and fixes before the @eslint/css upgrade.
decisions.rejected: Golden snapshots only

decisions.decision: Where does our plugin code live?
decisions.ruling: Inside this package: src/plugins/tailwindcss/ (index.ts, syntax.ts, types.ts, utils/, rules/), compiled into dist/ with the rest. Later plans add src/plugins/<name>/.
decisions.rejected: A separate npm package in a workspace

decisions.decision: Which language does the css preset use?
decisions.ruling: No own language. The css preset uses the css/css language of @eslint/css with our Tailwind syntax as customSyntax and tolerant: true. @eslint/css 2.0.0 adds meta.languages to its rules, so css/* rules run only on css/css. Our rules declare meta.languages ["css/css"].
decisions.rejected: Keep a tailwindcss/css language in our plugin (2.x rejects every css/* rule on it)

decisions.decision: How is parity proved before the upgrade?
decisions.ruling: U4 first switches the preset to our plugin on @eslint/css 1.4.0 and runs the golden tests: lint/problems.json and lint/fixes.json must not change, and config/file.css.json may change only in its language (tailwindcss/css to css/css) and by the removal of tailwindcss/require-reference-in-vue (D22). Then U4 upgrades to 2.0.1, so the later golden diff shows only the upgrade.
decisions.rejected: Port and upgrade in one step

decisions.decision: Does this change plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes, one review unit after U4. The change lands runnable code: about 3,500 lines of rule source shipped in the package.
decisions.rejected: Wave review only

decisions.decision: Execution mode
decisions.ruling: teams: wave 2 has two edit units (the two rule groups), which can message each other about shared helpers. If a team cannot start, the run uses solo.
decisions.rejected: solo

decisions.decision: Do we list the type-only packages @eslint/css-tree and @eslint/core?
decisions.ruling: Add both as exact-pinned devDependencies, at the versions that @eslint/css 2.0.1 resolves. They add nothing to the tarball. Justification: tsc must not depend on how pnpm hoists a transitive package. Imports from them are type-only (import type).
decisions.rejected: Do not list them (rely on nodeLinker hoisted); own type definitions

decisions.decision: Where does the rule configuration live?
decisions.ruling: In the css preset, not in the plugin. The plugin index (src/plugins/tailwindcss/index.ts, written by U4) exports meta and rules only (no configs, no languages); it merges the rule registries rules/group-a.ts (U2) and rules/group-b.ts (U3). The preset reproduces the rule severities and the rule options of the poupe recommended config exactly, except that it does not set tailwindcss/require-reference-in-vue (D22). It keeps files ["**/*.css"]: extends intersects the poupe glob **/*.?(post)css with the preset glob, so the current preset lints .css files only. The language follows D8.
decisions.rejected: configs.recommended inside our plugin; a plugin index created early by U1 (two units would then own one file)

decisions.decision: Where do the rule units get the source to port?
decisions.ruling: From the TypeScript source of github.com/poupe-ui/eslint-plugin-tailwindcss at tag v0.3.1, read with gh api (src/rules, src/utils, src/types.ts, src/__tests__). Not from the bundled dist in node_modules.
decisions.rejected: Port from the bundled node_modules dist

decisions.decision: Is the release level MINOR?
decisions.ruling: MINOR for @virajp.dev/linter: new rule behavior from @eslint/css 2.x, the removal of the tailwindcss/css language, and the removal of the Vue-only rule tailwindcss/require-reference-in-vue, which no consumer config names; no other rule name changes.
decisions.rejected: MAJOR (no rule name or preset name changes); PATCH

decisions.decision: How do we port prefer-logical-properties, relative-font-units and use-layers, which upstream only re-exports from @eslint/css?
decisions.ruling: Wrap the core rule: a new object that spreads the @eslint/css rule and sets meta.languages ["css/css"] (a new meta object, so the shared core object stays unchanged). The rules follow @eslint/css after the 2.x upgrade, as they do upstream today.
decisions.rejected: Copy the 1.4.0 source of each core rule into the repo

decisions.decision: What does U4 do when the @eslint/css 2.0.1 upgrade breaks tsc in a file that U1 to U3 wrote?
decisions.ruling: U4 may edit files under src/plugins/tailwindcss/ only to fix compile errors that the upgrade causes, with no change in behavior, and reports each as DECIDED. The review unit checks them. U4 creates src/plugins/tailwindcss/index.ts in the same directory.
decisions.rejected: U4 stops with a QUESTION

decisions.decision: Does THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md get an entry for tailwind-csstree, which syntax.ts uses as a reference with no copied code?
decisions.ruling: Yes. An acknowledgement section with the Apache-2.0 license text of tailwind-csstree (the version read, 0.3.3), its repository, and its author as its package.json writes it, worded as a reference, not as copied code. Its LICENSE has no copyright line, so the section adds none.
decisions.rejected: No entry, as syntax.ts is original work

decisions.decision: What happens when @eslint/css 2.x reports a new problem on tests/fixtures/css/valid.css?
decisions.ruling: U7 owns tests/fixtures/css/valid.css. It may change only the CSS that the new problem reports, keeps the CSS features the file has (modern syntax, so a parser regression still shows), and reports the change. It writes the golden snapshots after the fix.
decisions.rejected: Stop with a QUESTION

decisions.decision: Does a changed tailwindcss/ problem in the golden diff after the upgrade pass?
decisions.ruling: Only when its rule wraps or reuses an @eslint/css rule (D16). Any other tailwindcss/ change stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Accept every change after the upgrade

decisions.decision: Who updates a ported rule test whose expected result the @eslint/css 2.0.1 upgrade changes?
decisions.ruling: U4 may change the expected results in tests of rules that wrap or reuse an @eslint/css rule (D16 and the wrappers in utils/css.ts), only where the upgrade changes them, and reports each as DECIDED. The review unit checks them. A failure in any other rule test stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Stop with a QUESTION for every failing ported test

decisions.decision: Do we port the Vue-only rule tailwindcss/require-reference-in-vue? (revision of 2026-11-22, after approval)
decisions.ruling: No. The user never uses Vue: a scan of ~/Projects on 2026-11-22 found .vue files only in a third-party clone (tmp/mise), no Vue dependency in any package.json, and no Vue rule in any of the 25 .config/linter.yaml files. Do not port the rule or its test, and the preset does not set it. Plan 2 drops yml/vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error by the same ruling.
decisions.rejected: Port it as approved

decisions.decision: Who formats the files before the check-only unit gate? (revision of 2026-11-22, from the rulings review of plan 2)
decisions.ruling: Each edit unit runs mise x -- mise run code:format --fix before it returns, so that the unit gate (code:format, check only) passes.
decisions.rejected: A --fix unit gate

decisions.decision: What does a unit do when a ported upstream test fails only because ESLint 10 or vitest is stricter? (ruled by the user on 2026-11-22 for all B08 plans)
decisions.ruling: A ported upstream test case that fails only because ESLint 10's RuleTester or the vitest wiring is stricter than upstream's setup (jest on ESLint 9) — not because the rule behaves differently — may have its test setup changed: for example, remove a duplicate case, or add a property that ESLint 10 requires. Never change the expected messages, message ids, locations, output or suggestions. List each change as DECIDED; the review unit checks them. A case whose expected result differs stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Stop and ask for each case; apply it to one plan only

decisions.decision: How are eslint-disable comments for unknown rules and strict-TypeScript errors in ported code handled?
decisions.ruling: (a) A ported file may drop an eslint-disable or eslint-enable comment that names a rule this repo does not define, or rewrite it to the rule of this repo that it means; ESLint 10 reports an unknown rule in such a comment as an error, so code:lint would fail. (b) Where the repo's strict TypeScript (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, .js import extensions) rejects ported code, a unit fixes it only with changes that have no runtime effect: non-null assertions, casts, type annotations, import type, and .js or /index.js on relative imports. No runtime guard is added. List each kind of change as DECIDED. (Ruled for all B08 plans on 2026-11-22, from the rulings review of plan 6.)
decisions.rejected: Define the unknown rules; add runtime guards

decisions.decision: Q1: Must a new test file for a Tailwind rule that has no upstream test start with a header line?
decisions.ruling: Use U2's "// New test: ..." line in all 5 new test files (U3 adds it to its 4 files) — every test file names its relation to upstream and the files are consistent.
decisions.rejected: Use no header in a new test file (U2 removes its line) — D5 covers only ported files, and new files carry no upstream reference
